headline: HubSpot is laying off about 600 employees, 7% of its staff, as it reorganises around AI, though its chief executive says the cuts are not driven by AI savings.
score_reason: Lowered by one: the layoffs were announced about 6 Oct 2026 and this is a later report; the job count differs between outlets.
importance_line: About 600 HubSpot staff lose their jobs with 20 to 30 weeks of pay, and the company's revenue is growing, so the CEO's statement that AI is not behind the cuts is her own account.
summary: The American Bazaar reports that software company HubSpot is laying off about 600 employees, or 7% of its workforce, as it shifts to an AI-focused strategy, according to a letter from CEO Yamini Rangan. Rangan said the cuts are "not simply a cost-cutting exercise" or driven by AI efficiencies, and staff will receive at least 20 weeks of base pay in severance; other outlets reported the layoffs on 6 Oct 2026.
notes: Quartz and the Boston Globe reported the layoffs on 6 Oct 2026 (Quartz headline 660 jobs); the American Bazaar gives about 600.
